B2 cha 176: Well, you are someone who has made it this far. The frightening thing about /VAR/-sama is that I cannot quite dismiss it as a lie.

C1 cha 178: Hee hee, whatever happens, a person's tastes hardly ever change.
C2 cha 204: Of course, the food in Arata is wonderful too. But that is everyday food, so to speak.
C3 cha 218: It is precisely because pizza is something you eat only now and then that it has value.

キャプション1: Where did /立木/ come from?
A2 cha 341: I have come from Room 306, Revo Heights, 120-10 Nagaminedai, Motoki-cho, Sawa District, Sawa Prefecture.
キャプション2 cha 110: Put like that, it's super normal
B1 cha 226: Well... it is ordinary, isn't it. Of course it is; inside I am just a human being.
B2 cha 176: Back then you may have thought I came from somewhere far more amazing, but in a sense this world is the more amazing place.
B3 cha 212: This is the only place where /VAR/-sama and I can meet. I love Motoki-cho too, but in that sense this world is a very precious place to me as well.
C1 cha 178: Let me see, as for places not in the encyclopedia...
C2 cha 204: A nursery school opened nearby recently. With Motoki-cho's population growing, demand for facilities like that is rising, as you would expect.
C3 cha 218: I sometimes see lots of the nursery-school children. They are very cute. When I see the little ones toddling along, I stop in my tracks and grin.
C4 cha 215: Ah... it is not as if I have that sort of inclination. I simply think they are cute.
C5 cha 180: R-really, it's not that kind of thing, okay!? I just think little kids are cute! I'm not like a certain girl-loving detective!
C7 cha 205: What am I getting so flustered about...

キャプション1: What do you do while I am viewing a scenario?
A1 cha 242: Well, now that things are as they are, I shall be honest with you.
A2 cha 341: Up to the Saigo no Koe Arc [Last Voice], it was nothing but heartache. Even though I was looking back on a happy path, the reality that I had killed Natsumi was gradually sinking in.
A3 cha 205: So I somewhat regretted inviting a guest here. I would never see that Natsumi again, and my old life would never come back.
A4 cha 166: Making up for that, once I had bared my face I was desperate to chase the mysteries. I wanted to know what had driven me this far.
A5 cha 162: But when the lid came off, there were only each person's own painful feelings. No great ambition or malice had been at work.
A6 cha 159: Personal feelings like those turned into events that large. It brought home to me how frightening human beings are.
A7 cha 142: The human heart is beautiful and frightening at once. All the more so when love or justice gets tangled up in it.
A8 cha 133: The ethics by which humankind tries to be in the right must be an eternal theme.

キャプション1: How many scenarios are there in all?
A1 cha 242: The Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse] has 46, at 192,852 characters. The Meicho Arc [Clear Sign] has 20, at 90,998 characters. The Wabigoto Arc [Apology] has 20, at 99,120 characters; the Shigatsu Arc [Death Month] has 57, at 278,081 characters.
A2 cha 341: The Saigo no Koe Arc [Last Voice] has 10, at 58,017 characters. The True Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse] has 7, at 518,444 characters. The True Meicho Arc [Clear Sign] has 2, at 3,118 characters. The Eden no Sakura Arc [Eden's Cherry] has 53, at 355,445 characters. The Eigo Kaiki Arc [Eternal Recurrence] has 5, at roughly 10,000 characters.
A3 cha 205: That is about 1.61 million characters in total. This does not include the hidden routes, references, encyclopedia, chats or system text, so the grand total would be about 2.4 million characters, I suppose.
キャプション2 cha 110: How many more hidden routes will there be?
キャプション5: What are hidden routes in the first place?
B1 cha 226: How many more there will be...
B2 cha 176: As you know, I understand this world no better than /VAR/-sama does.
B3 cha 212: This world has become one that reflects /VAR/-sama's mind as well.
B4 cha 182: If you show that will in some form, clearly and plainly, there may be more.
B5 cha 171: How you make that will clear I leave to /VAR/-sama.

C2 cha 204: But as you know, there seem to be secrets still unknown.
C3 cha 218: When and in what form they will appear before us, I do not know, but...
C4 cha 215: As long as /VAR/-sama keeps the will to know the truth beyond that, this world will have room to change.
D1 cha 142: Oh my, /VAR/-sama, how greedy you are.
D2 cha 217: But that you have enjoyed this world so much makes me as happy as can be.
D3 cha 211: This world seems to be changing little by little even now. Hidden routes appearing, more topics to talk about with me like this.
D4 cha 227: I would like you to watch over how this world changes for years to come.
E1 cha 166: It seems they let you view scenarios you have already seen from another person's viewpoint.
E2 cha 174: So I believe even the behind-the-scenes circumstances that the main story alone left unclear are shown plainly.
E3 cha 191: And besides changing the viewpoint, they seem to hide secrets that had never been revealed until now.
E4 cha 278: Very rarely, a hidden route may turn out to be a scenario deeper and more difficult than the main story, but...
E5 cha 220: Well, the hidden routes are a sort of reward for /VAR/-sama, who has come to like this world so much.
E6 cha 175: I would ask you to think of them strictly as a bonus.

キャプション1: How long will /立木/ be staying here?
A1 cha 242: I believe you already know, but I will stay for as long as /VAR/-sama wishes me to exist.
A2 cha 341: Even if I go to another dimension, even if I return to my own world, so long as /VAR/-sama wants to see me: forever.
キャプション2 cha 110: I feel like I'm tying /立木/ down
キャプション3 cha 104: Are you happy to see me?
B1 cha 226: Yes, it would look that way from /VAR/-sama's point of view.
B2 cha 176: But in this world, time stops the moment /VAR/-sama is gone.
B3 cha 212: So it is not that I am left waiting for /VAR/-sama in vain all the while; on the contrary, I regard myself as always being with /VAR/-sama.
B4 cha 182: So please do not think of it as tying me down, and come whenever you like.
B5 cha 171: /VAR/-sama is someone precious to me as well.
C1 cha 178: Of course I am. You kept me company from beginning to end and always cared about me.
C2 cha 204: /VAR/-sama's coming here is itself my greatest joy.

キャプション1: What kind of world is this in the first place?
A2 cha 341: That may well be the greatest mystery of all.
A3 cha 205: Before, I told you this place was something like the inside of my dream, and indeed it does not seem very different from a dream.
A4 cha 166: I cannot define where this is... What does /VAR/-sama think?
キャプション2 cha 110: /立木/'s dream and my mind are connected
キャプション4 cha 114: Something else entirely is the cause
B1 cha 226: Oh my... my mind and /VAR/-sama's...
B2 cha 176: That is a little embarrassing. But the fact that /VAR/-sama and I really are connected like this...
B3 cha 212: Hmm... is it because it was /VAR/-sama, after all, that you connected with my mind? Because it was /VAR/-sama and no one else.
B5 cha 171: W-wait, let us leave it at that... It is too embarrassing to talk about any further...
C1 cha 178: Caused by Shigatsu Youka...?
C2 cha 204: Hmm, it is true that Shigatsu Youka has the power to show phantoms, and the real me is still third generation.
C3 cha 218: So the possibility that it is Shigatsu Youka's doing cannot be ruled out.
C4 cha 215: But even for Shigatsu Youka, is it really possible to show someone events in another dimension?
C5 cha 180: Besides, precisely because I saw a course of events like the Eden no Sakura Arc [Eden's Cherry], destroying the Shigatsu Youka of my own dimension is possible too.
C6 cha 237: There are things that make it rather hard to explain with Shigatsu Youka as the cause. But it is frightening, too, that I cannot say it is 100% not.
C7 cha 205: Perhaps Shigatsu Youka still holds mysteries yet to be solved.

D2 cha 217: Hmm, does /VAR/-sama know the concept called 'the brain in a vat'?

D4 cha 227: In other words, both the me in this world and the me in my original world are merely being shown a virtual reality, and the body no longer exists. It would mean being nothing but a guinea pig.
D5 cha 198: Oh? Then would that mean /VAR/-sama, who is in this world, is in the same vat as me?
D6 cha 232: There is no way to prove whether the reality /VAR/-sama sees is truly reality.
D7 cha 175: If so, you would be living in the same vat as me practically forever.

A4 cha 166: If it is a world of dreams, then the timeline, dimensions, everything is as one likes.

C3 cha 218: But I almost never have lucid dreams. I usually only realize it was a dream once I wake up.

C5 cha 180: Hmm, if anything it seems closer to /VAR/-sama's dream. /VAR/-sama originally came here out of interest in the stories that unfold here.
C6 cha 237: Even so, there must have been events and changes in this world that /VAR/-sama never imagined, so defining this world does seem quite difficult after all.

A1 cha 242: Honestly, it is not that there is any particular connection.
A2 cha 341: Or so I told you before.
A3 cha 205: Looking back now, how embarrassing. As you know, there is a connection, a big one, a super-big one.

B4 cha 182: But in the end, I never had the courage.
B5 cha 171: When you found out the fact that I had killed Natsumi, I made up my mind.

B7 cha 169: Whether I would have waited until the next guest appeared, or been alone in this world forever, unable to bear the guilt.

B9 cha 120: Above all, you have kept me company this far. I cannot thank you enough.

C5 cha 180: Looking back with someone, far from sharing a happy feeling, I ended up feeling even more pain.
C6 cha 237: So I came to think that once the 'Saigo no Koe' Arc [Last Voice] was over, I would ask /VAR/-sama to leave as soon as possible.

キャプション1: Any tips for viewing the references well?
A1 cha 242: Hmmm... it is rather late to say, but let me see...
A2 cha 341: There were probably references that made you wonder, 'What did this mean?' Especially the ones whose person is listed as 'Unknown'.
A3 cha 205: Among those with the person unknown, there are many cases where the viewpoint belongs to someone who could not be revealed when it unlocked but whose name has already appeared.
A4 cha 166: And then the date and time. Your reading may change greatly depending on when it takes place.
A5 cha 162: The person and the date and time: if you go back over them with these two points in mind, you may make unexpected discoveries.

キャプション1: Are there any special controls? 1
A1 cha 242: As for what I can tell you at this point... It turns into something of a talk about the system, but―
A2 cha 341: For comfortable play, several save files are generated in the background. As the save data grows larger, loading times get slightly longer.
A3 cha 205: /VAR/-sama cannot delete these system save files by hand, but a special procedure can reduce their size.
A4 cha 166: Do this: start the game → delete the save.dat file → quit the game. The save data should become a good deal smaller.
A5 cha 162: However, since this touches the save data directly, there is no telling what trouble may occur. Please do it strictly at your own risk.
A6 cha 159: Never forget to back up your save data.
A7 cha 142: Well, even if you reduce the size, the system save data is generated again soon after, so it doesn't really mean much.

キャプション1: Are there any special controls? 2
A1 cha 242: Are you backing up your save data? The save.dat file is the save data.
A2 cha 341: In case of emergency, you can copy this save.dat file and keep it, which backs up the data as of that moment.
A3 cha 205: You may name the copied data however you like, and there is no problem at all with keeping it inside the game folder.
A4 cha 166: I think it best to keep backup data whenever you can, so do give it a try.

キャプション1: Are there any special controls? 3
A1 cha 242: This game saves automatically, so the latest state is saved even when you close the game.
A2 cha 341: Put the other way round, it is impossible to keep an earlier state saved.
A3 cha 205: If you do not want it to autosave over the earlier state, choose to force-end the process in the Windows Task Manager. The game will close without autosaving.

キャプション1: Tell me something interesting 1
A1 cha 242: Eh... you ask that, at this stage...
A2 cha 341: Well then, since you asked, I would like to share as much of the behind-the-scenes story of this work's making as I am able to tell.
キャプション2 cha 110: How the scenarios were made
B1 cha 226: As the afterword touched on, it was made almost entirely off the cuff. Writing down whatever came to mind at the time, on and on―
B2 cha 176: Honestly, it was made without even the creator having any idea what kind of story it would become. No plot outline exists either.
B3 cha 212: At first only Natsumi and I appeared, but on a sudden whim the creator decided we would 'meet a silly little junior in Chuo Park'. That is Goto.
B4 cha 182: So if not for that passing whim, Goto might never have existed.
B5 cha 171: I said 'silly junior', and at first Goto was set up to be extremely stupid. But with three below-average people talking, the story never came together at all―
B6 cha 212: So, again out of nowhere, Goto was given the setting of a genius girl. The idea being that with Goto around, the mysteries could be written with ease.
B7 cha 169: That is why, once the Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse] is some way along, the story proceeds from Goto's viewpoint. That is purely to make things easier for the creator...
B8 cha 193: Well, the scenarios of this world went on being made in this spirit right to the very end. From the creator's point of view, they are fairly patched-together scenarios.
C1 cha 178: The hardest part was none other than 'this'.
C2 cha 204: Yes, the chats. Building the system and writing out the topics were both hard enough to nearly bring one to tears, apparently.
C3 cha 218: After all, as many as 500 chat topics with me had to be thought up. It seems the creator feels a lack of ability for having squeezed in some padded-looking topics now and then.
C4 cha 215: The creator often puts it this way: 'Could you think up as many as 500 topics for someone at a group date?' To me it is a case of "What is this person even talking about," but anyway, it was apparently very hard.
C5 cha 180: Around the fall of 2018, the creator apparently spent about 2 months doing nothing but writing out topics for me.
C6 cha 237: Incidentally, the chats come to about 250,000 characters of text. That is about 1.3 times the Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse].
C7 cha 205: If I were given a voice, the playback time would apparently come to more than 13 hours by calculation.
D1 cha 142: Well, there are a lot of characters, so I cannot introduce them all...
D2 cha 217: Then let me introduce my grandmother, the cosplay hag, Erika Niimura.
D3 cha 211: My grandmother first came up in the Meicho Arc [Clear Sign], where I succeeded in catching Mom by doing an impression of my grandmother.
D4 cha 227: At that point, the creator apparently thought: "Haruka Niimura being able to do impressions is way too convenient."
D5 cha 198: At first my grandmother's character concept was a thoroughly suspicious head of the settlement, someone with truly root-of-all-evil sort of thinking.
D6 cha 232: But because of the impression business, that concept was changed drastically, and she became the person you know: a lover of cosplay and anime, and a pacifist besides.
D7 cha 175: Like this, the character concepts too were changed again and again for the convenience of the scenarios.

キャプション1: Tell me something interesting 2
A1 cha 242: Let me see... having come this far, there really is nothing left to talk about but the behind-the-scenes story...
A2 cha 341: These, then, are people whose character concepts were changed a great deal, so let me explain how they changed.
キャプション2 cha 110: Haruka Niimura
B1 cha 226: I shall explain how the character concept of myself, Haruka Niimura, changed.
B2 cha 176: At first I was just a friend who lived next door to Natsumi, with no concept beyond that whatsoever.
B3 cha 212: So my age, way of speaking and personality were almost the same as Natsumi's. Apart from my image color being blue, I had truly no individuality at all.
B4 cha 182: The creator thought that would not do, and set out to distinguish me from Natsumi by forcing me to use boyish speech and cutting my hair short, I am told.
B5 cha 171: Incidentally, when production began, Natsumi, Goto and I were 4 years younger than now. I was in the second year of middle school, and Goto in sixth grade.
B6 cha 212: But it was decided that this made it hard to have us understand complicated matters, so our ages were raised to the current settings.
B7 cha 169: Seen this way, high school is a truly convenient age group for production, as the creator seems to have learned the hard way.
B8 cha 193: Incidentally, the reason my chest is large is apparently that the creator wanted to show cleavage when the person inside was revealed and made to bow. Apparently that really is the only reason.
B9 cha 120: Jeez... try putting yourself in my shoes...
C1 cha 178: Next, I shall explain how the character of my cousin Kana changed.
C2 cha 204: At first, Kana was Chiga-nee's mother and Kotaro-san's wife. She stood where Sakura-san does. To me, that would have made her Aunt Kana.
C3 cha 218: As Aunt Kana, unlike Sakura-san she was not dead even on the Shigatsu Arc [Death Month] routes, and was a bride who came from outside, like Mom, but...
C4 cha 215: Because Aunt Kana had far too little individuality, and the Shigatsu Arc [Death Month] itself was judged hopelessly dull, large-scale construction work was carried out.
C5 cha 180: With that, Sakura-san took Aunt Kana's place, and only the name remained, so that my cousin Kana came to appear.
C6 cha 237: Making Kana a child was fine, but telling her apart from Goto as a character seems to have been terribly hard, so the creator deliberately kept the two together for long stretches to find what set them apart.
D1 cha 142: Shirozaki-san is another person whose character changed quite a lot, but he was written along a theme that never wavered from start to finish.
D3 cha 211: Up to the third route of the Shigatsu Arc [Death Month], not a single resident of Arata apart from the Niimura family had appeared, so Shirozaki-san was written as the representative of the background residents.
D4 cha 227: But through riding a buggy to the convenience store with Natsumi, just the two of them, settings were gradually added: he lost his wife to the first curse-killing, he came to explain the residents' suspicion feeding on itself―
D5 cha 198: Once that happened, he had to be quite a good-hearted character, and he came to play important roles at key points, such as tipping Natsumi off that the residents were after her.
D6 cha 232: Even so, he never comes to the front of the story; it is more that he stays strictly a supporting player, though.
E1 cha 166: At first, Momoko Goto was conceived as a party girl who had quit high school, drifted around having fun, and went through men one after another.
E2 cha 174: So she was quite far from the easygoing figure she is now. Some of the original concept does remain, but much of that part is Goto's own assumption.
E3 cha 191: But a character like that was hard to involve with that group of people no matter what, so she was changed into an awkward personality who pushes her sister away and tends to isolate herself.
E4 cha 278: Even with that personality, her parents raised her with firm discipline, so she never forgets her manners toward others; she has been made into a split-personality sort of person who, once she puts on her best behavior, could call herself the shop's star girl even at Primavera.
E5 cha 220: Further, to make her easier to involve in the story, the trait of loving her sister dearly yet finding it hard to get close to her was added.

キャプション1: Tell me something interesting 3
A1 cha 242: This time, then, shall I explain how the elements other than the characters came about?
キャプション2 cha 110: Droga
B1 cha 226: You know how important Droga is to the story, but in fact it is an element added quite late.
B2 cha 176: Do you remember the third route of the Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse]? Though it was Goto's hallucination, it ends with the shinigami charging at Natsumi and slashing her neck.
B3 cha 212: While working out how the shinigami who met Natsumi and the others would go about killing, the creator apparently thought, "What a hassle, just have it kill with a high-speed dash! I'll think up the trick later!"
B4 cha 182: So, as a leftover of that, there are almost no scenes in the Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse] where Droga's effects are clear. Jumping from a roof, dodging bullets, that is about all.
B5 cha 171: At the time of the trial release published in February 2016, Droga did not even exist in the settings.
B6 cha 212: Well, so the trick of the Megasawa City case was still vague going into the Wabigoto Arc [Apology], and right at the last moment, when Mom had to explain the trick, the creator went, "Let's make it a drug"...
B7 cha 169: That is why the early part has a lot of scenario pacing that is brute force, or rather pushed through on momentum.
C1 cha 178: As for why Noh masks are used in this world...
C2 cha 204: There was no particular reason; at the shinigami's character design stage it was "Wouldn't something Japanese have more impact than a skull mask?", so a Noh mask was put on for the time being, apparently.
C3 cha 218: So coming up with a reason for the shinigami to wear a Noh mask was apparently a real struggle. Even if it is the traditional dress of the Arata settlement, then why did it become tradition?
C4 cha 215: Noh masks actually became popular right around the Warring States period, so the custom of wearing them was set as beginning then, and if so, there must have been some big event in the Arata settlement at that time.
C5 cha 180: That big event is the invention of Droga and the first Arata Incident that it caused.
C6 cha 237: In the story, the true reason is that it is an item for preventing the Green-Eye Curse-Killing, but that setting too came from thinking, how could anyone fight the Shigatsu Youka that held Itohime captive?
C7 cha 205: Well, by chance there had been a rule from the start that danger sense requires seeing a face or hearing a voice, and that came to the rescue. The creator was apparently very grateful to their own setting.
D1 cha 142: The setting of the place called the Arata settlement was decided at a very early stage.
D2 cha 217: First, the Megasawa City case occurred every few years, and Dad's memorial service was used to manufacture an alibi for it.
D3 cha 211: So it had to be a settlement mixing in not only the Buddhist third-year and seventh-year memorial services but also Shinto culture, with its tenth-year rite, but...
D4 cha 227: On top of that, the Western culture of the 'shinigami', the Grim Reaper, was needed too, so the foundation came together: a settlement that is insular despite its tendency to take in many cultures.
D5 cha 198: Missionaries came in the Muromachi period, and other people with all sorts of ideas came too. Going on like this, the Arata settlement becomes a crystallization of cultures from all ages and places.
D6 cha 232: But for people to put down roots in a settlement deep in the mountains, the place needed some appeal. For people long ago, a place where food was never short seemed best, the creator thought.
D7 cha 175: And then it must surely have faced the threat of invasion again and again. So it settled on being insular, yet multicultural and warlike.
D8 cha 201: Unusually for this work, its settings were hardly changed.
E1 cha 166: I, the guide, did not exist in the trial release published in February 2016.
E2 cha 174: The trial release received all sorts of feedback, including that the ending came suddenly and felt abrupt, and that it was hard to tell how the story was meant to progress...
E3 cha 191: To improve those points, the guide was introduced.
E4 cha 278: Then how does it end? Who is the guide? Such questions came up one after another, so the creator decided to make the guide one of the main characters.
E5 cha 220: And so the lot fell on me, Haruka Niimura.
E6 cha 175: And for that setting, even a scenario where I stab Natsumi to death was added... What a truly awful creator.
E7 cha 172: If the trial release had not received that feedback, I would not exist, and I would never have chatted with /VAR/-sama like this.
E8 cha 169: I am truly indebted to everyone who left a review.

キャプション1: What is a letters reference?
A1 cha 242: These are writings left by people of the past whom the main story cannot fully cover. As you know, very important things are written in them.
A2 cha 341: However, even at this point there are a few where it is hard to tell what they are talking about. Let me explain some of them myself.
キャプション2 cha 110: No.31 The Head of the Exalted One
B1 cha 226: This was touched on briefly in 'My Heart to You.' of the Eden no Sakura Arc [Eden's Cherry].
B2 cha 176: It means that Prince Mochihito, after leaving the Arata settlement, was killed by the remnants of the Tara clan, as in the letter.
B3 cha 212: Unfortunately, in the Motoki lands of the time there was a man who had served at the Imperial Palace. Weighing Taira no Kiyomori's military strength, he turned traitor.
B4 cha 182: Expecting a great reward from Kiyomori, he struck down Prince Mochihito, but...
B5 cha 171: The letter was written in 1188. By then, Kiyomori had already passed away.
B6 cha 212: So there was no way he could get a reward, and the times were tilting toward the Minamoto clan.
B7 cha 169: So what became of him is uncertain, but perhaps he was executed.
B8 cha 193: In those days news did not reach the provinces, so he must have struck down Prince Mochihito without knowing Kiyomori was dead.
C1 cha 178: It seems to have been written by a resident of Arata in 1599.
C2 cha 204: The same thing happens in 'Kill the Goddess Kill Them All' of the True Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse]. In other words, it is about people who became the fourth generation.
C3 cha 218: In 1598 the first Green-Eye Curse-Killing occurred, and it grew into a fight between the residents and the missionaries. Droga was being used, so new second and third generations were born.
C4 cha 215: Naturally, among those who survived the fight there were first and second generations, but they must have taken in spores when they buried those who had become third generation.
C5 cha 180: As a result, they were infected by Shigatsu Youka's spores, doted on the third-generation corpses until they rotted, and a year later became Shigatsu Youka's seedbeds completely.
C6 cha 237: Then they moved to a place suited for breeding and became fruiting bodies of Shigatsu Youka.
C7 cha 205: The bodies disappeared most likely because they touched the petals and were digested as nutrients. It is a phenomenon also seen in 'Parasite Prison' of the True Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse].
C8 cha 152: In this way, it is a letter that records Shigatsu Youka's breeding process.
D1 cha 142: This letter describes a means of fighting Shigatsu Youka. The young Grand Witch of that time became third generation through some chance.
D2 cha 217: Somehow she realized her blood could damage Shigatsu Youka, and tried to defeat it using all of her blood.
D3 cha 211: But as Itohime said, the blood of a single human was not enough; she lost her life, yet it was not enough to drive it off completely.
D4 cha 227: Still, the damage to Shigatsu Youka was by no means small, it seems, and I believe it went quiet again for a while in order to breed.
D5 cha 198: Because of such wisdom and sacrifice by our ancestors, Shigatsu Youka was finally defeated in 2020.
D6 cha 232: It was most likely an even more harrowing event than the letter records. I would like to see how it happened myself.
D7 cha 175: Incidentally, No.87 'Picture of the Demon Flower' was made by companions of the Grand Witch who was sacrificed.
E1 cha 166: Small as the Arata settlement's population is, not every single person thinks the same.
E2 cha 174: This letter must have been written by someone who hated Kikyo-san for banning Droga and sealing away the Verde mummy.
E3 cha 191: To begin with, throwing away what you have worshipped until now is not easy.
E4 cha 278: Even though it was the order of Kikyo-san, the Grand Witch, there must have been more than a few who felt rebellious.
E5 cha 220: All the more so when even Droga, an important hunting tool, was taken away; it is no wonder they felt hostility.
E6 cha 175: Fascination is a frightening thing. Be it an idol or a tool, having it suddenly taken away leaves hatred behind.
E7 cha 172: The writer probably never acted openly, but I think it symbolizes that the Arata settlement is not united.
E8 cha 169: But in the Eden no Sakura Arc [Eden's Cherry], everyone came together as one and destroyed Shigatsu Youka.
E9 cha 216: So I believe that even if their ways of thinking differ, at the root everyone is connected.

キャプション1: What is a report reference?
A1 cha 242: It is a report on human experiments with Droga, written by Hajime Shinozaki, who belonged to the Holy Cerejeira Church.
A2 cha 341: Here too, as before, let me explain the ones that are hard to understand.
キャプション2 cha 110: Danger sense for an instant
B1 cha 226: Danger sense for an instant―to give a concrete example, it is what happened to Goto in 'Third Generation' of the True Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse]. For just an instant, she foresaw what would happen in the Arata settlement.
B2 cha 176: This is recorded in No.22 'Treating the Curse-Killing'. To be infected with Droga, the mucous membranes of the head must touch 1 ml or more of an infected person's blood.
B3 cha 212: But if it is under 1 ml, the spores are expelled by metabolism within seconds, and the infection is incomplete.
B4 cha 182: What happened to Goto then was this symptom, and in the mere seconds between infection and expulsion she had that much danger sense.
B5 cha 171: However, being able to learn so much about people other than the one in danger is a phenomenon far outside regular danger sense.
B6 cha 212: In the first place, danger sense is originally meant for Shigatsu Youka to communicate with its divine messengers. In other words, anything within what Shigatsu Youka knows can be sent to the infected.
B7 cha 169: So information about Arata and future danger got all jumbled together, and on top of that, expulsion from the body, which means death to the spores, was about to happen.
B8 cha 193: Such extremely irregular circumstances overlapping is probably why such danger sense was possible.
C1 cha 178: Normally, the Green-Eye Curse-Killing makes the third generation kill someone with danger sense without even giving them time to think.
C2 cha 204: Like when I killed Natsumi, or like Momoko Goto in 'Memory × Revenge × Tumor' of the True Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse]. We could not even resist the murderous intent.
C3 cha 218: But Kana in 'Memory × Revenge × Tumor' of the True Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse], and Tomi, who became the Verde mummy, resisted that murderous intent and had room to run away or kill themselves.
C4 cha 215: Why such a difference arose is recorded in No.21, Methods of Suppressing the Urge to Kill.
C5 cha 180: Those roughly 15 or under have less developed nervous systems than adults, so the murderous urge from Shigatsu Youka is apparently not complete.
C6 cha 237: So there is about a 30 percent chance they can resist that murderous intent. Though even then they apparently end up killing the target in the end.
D1 cha 142: What is April sickness in the first place? That too is written in the reports. No.8, Trauma in the Second Generation.
D2 cha 217: According to it, even when the second generation was infected in a situation where trauma was very unlikely to arise, recreating the circumstances of that time made them unwell; that is, they fell into April sickness.
D3 cha 211: So one can say for certain that April sickness is caused not by trauma but by Shigatsu Youka.
D4 cha 227: However, there are also cases where April sickness goes into remission if the second generation suffers some emotional damage when infected. Like Natsumi on the Shigatsu Arc [Death Month] routes.
D5 cha 198: This is probably because April sickness was disguised as trauma. It would be unnatural for the trauma to continue even after Natsumi had accepted my dad's death.
D6 cha 232: In the first place, the reason Shigatsu Youka needs April sickness is thought to be to secure the safety of the second generation.
D7 cha 175: The second generation are the ones who give birth to the third generation, which spreads the infection, and they also hold danger sense, which maintains the safety of society.
D8 cha 201: So the surrounding society protects the second generation carefully. But the third generation is the opposite. To Shigatsu Youka, the third generation are individuals it wants dead as soon as possible.
D9 cha 153: Therefore, by having them try to kill the precious second generation, a cycle is established in which the surrounding society kills the third generation.
E1 cha 166: As written in No.24, How the Eyes Turn Green, this is probably simply to make it easy for the surrounding society to tell who is third generation.
E2 cha 174: For a society that uses Droga, the third generation are very dangerous. After all, they try to kill the precious second generation.
E3 cha 191: The old law of the Arata settlement said that a girl born with green eyes was to be killed at once. That law, one could say, was entirely Shigatsu Youka's trap.
E4 cha 278: When the third generation die like this, spores that give rise to the fourth generation are released from their bodies. For Shigatsu Youka, it is a very convenient life cycle.
E5 cha 220: However, the third generation only began turning green-eyed after the Arata settlement was founded. Before then there were no humans, but in animal societies third-generation killings of their own kind were taking place.
E6 cha 175: That could be seen in 'Arata: A New Village' of the Eden no Sakura Arc [Eden's Cherry]. The deer killing each other was precisely the Green-Eye Curse-Killing.
E7 cha 172: But Shigatsu Youka, having no intelligence then, could not make the third generation 'stand out'. That came after Shigatsu Youka merged with Itohime.
E8 cha 169: That must be why Itohime's eye color became the very mark of the Green-Eye Curse-Killing.
E9 cha 216: After gaining intelligence, Shigatsu Youka seems to have searched for a way to overcome that weakness in order to live on forever.

キャプション1: What is a side-tale reference?
A1 cha 242: The main ones are scenarios focusing on the life of Kikyo, a girl who moved from Edo to the Arata settlement.
A2 cha 341: Let me explain some of them myself.
キャプション2 cha 110: About Kikyo's family home
キャプション3 cha 104: About the Arata settlement back then

B4 cha 182: In the midst of that, she married into the Arata settlement by the shogun's order, so Kikyo's family home was able to receive the shogunate's protection.

B6 cha 212: In fact, this Konoe Zaibatsu does not appear at all this time, but in the next―
B7 cha 169: Oops, I cannot tell you any more yet. This is top secret. Hee hee hee.
C1 cha 178: If you look at letter No.195 'The Flow of the Times' and side tale No.16 'The Life of an Accomplished Woman: Accepting Contradiction', you should be able to guess to some extent.
C2 cha 204: Some years before Kikyo married in, a mass disappearance occurred in the Arata settlement. And new cherry trees were found, as many as the people who vanished.
C3 cha 218: This was Shigatsu Youka's doing, but the Grand Witch of the time, that is, Akira Niimura's mother, tried to unravel this mystery through scholarship.
C4 cha 215: To that end, she had her son Akira take Droga to an audience with the shogun, planning to research Droga with the shogunate's money.
C5 cha 180: So it is not hard to imagine that until Kikyo married in, the air was very tense. After all, 30 people had disappeared.
C6 cha 237: Though the shogun did not accept the Droga, the arrival of a bride from outside, a bright event for the first time in a long while, brought the settlement back to life.
C7 cha 205: The disappearances started, as No.194 'The Sealed Goddess' showed, from one of the residents happening to find the Verde mummy.
C8 cha 152: From around 1600, Droga was used and banned over and over, and the Arata settlement faced extinction several times. As they say, history repeats itself.
D1 cha 142: Kikyo is killed by her husband Akira, who had become a divine messenger.
D2 cha 217: Probably because Shigatsu Youka judged that Kikyo could not be left alone any longer. That is why Kikyo alone, as an exception, died in February.
D3 cha 211: And this had not yet been revealed in the main story, but the reason Arata residents always die in April is Droga.
D4 cha 227: Almost every Arata resident of the time had used Droga. So anyone who has used Droga dies in April, even if it is of illness.
D5 cha 198: Goto made a similar analysis in 'Solved (Tentative)' of the Shigatsu Arc [Death Month].
D6 cha 232: April is when the Arata cherry's spores are most active. That is, the spores' metabolic activity was putting a load on the bodies of the elderly.
E1 cha 166: That would be the person called the sect's Director. He went by Tsuchida, but his real name is unknown. Probably he changed his family register, like Shinozaki.
E2 cha 174: They secretly tried to push ahead with research into Shigatsu Youka. What came of that was the public research group in Motoki-cho.
E3 cha 191: But the research group was beaten to death in their lodgings, and the plan fell through. So Tsuchida approached Shinozaki and urged him to slip research reports into the settlement.
E4 cha 278: As the side-tale references showed, Shinozaki had stood at the forefront of the research, so he had very vivid memories of Shigatsu Youka, and wrote the reports again.
E5 cha 220: Tsuchida's true reason for approaching Shinozaki was to obtain those reports. After the war, all of Shinozaki's reports had been destroyed to keep the research data from being seized.
E6 cha 175: With that, much of the research results did, in a sense, come back into the Director's hands, but...
E7 cha 172: On the other hand, through a misunderstanding Shinozaki came to be rumored a villain, and since he had become more conspicuous than necessary, he had to be disposed of.
E8 cha 169: His drawing public attention would have been a very grave matter for the state as well. After all, the sect had ties to the state, so having him stand out was a problem.
E9 cha 216: After disposing of him, Tsuchida killed himself too. So only the upper echelons of the state knew of Shigatsu Youka's existence, and in 2029 the International Research Institute was founded with Goto as its director.

キャプション1: /立木/: student? Working adult?
A1 cha 242: I am a third-year at Sawa Prefectural High School.
A2 cha 341: Come to think of it, the main story hardly talks about school. Is there anything you would like to ask?
キャプション2 cha 110: Is it a smart high school?
キャプション4 cha 114: What kind of teachers are there?
B1 cha 226: Its deviation score is 47. Well, it is not that smart a school.
B2 cha 176: That is because most of the students come from middle schools in Motoki-cho. I do not think it is a high school people choose by how smart they are.
B3 cha 212: You cannot get in if your conduct is truly bad or your entrance exam is a total disaster, but the atmosphere is not that different from elementary and middle school.
B4 cha 182: So right after enrolling you have a meeting with a teacher and are asked whether you are thinking of getting a job or going on to further education after graduating.
B5 cha 171: Mom had told me to go on to further education, so I said I wanted to go to university.
B6 cha 212: But changing course partway through is not unusual, so they give career guidance suited to the student each time. In that respect I think it is kinder than a prep school that only cares about university entrance.
B7 cha 169: Also, the students' grades vary a great deal, so every year a few get into famous universities.
B8 cha 193: In that sense, I think it is a very flexible school. I like my school.
C1 cha 178: Unusual events... let me see... I have never compared it with other schools, so nothing comes to mind right away, but...
C2 cha 204: We do not have cherry-blossom viewing just because the cherries are famous, and there is no volunteer activity of planting cherry trees either. Then, as for something you could call an unusual event―
C3 cha 218: Ah, yes, that's it! There is a social studies activity of visiting nursery schools and elementary schools. It is an event where, as seniors living in Motoki-cho, we tell the little children how wonderful Motoki-cho is.
C4 cha 215: I went to a nursery school in the summer of my second year. The high schoolers stay overnight at the nursery school too, to match the nursery school's sleepover. That must be quite rare, I would think.
C5 cha 180: We have barbecues and watermelon splitting with the children, and at night we sit around a campfire. Not just the children, but the high schoolers get excited too.
C6 cha 237: Yes, I remembered there was an event like that when I was at nursery school too. It is less a school event than something like a Motoki-cho tradition that has gone on for decades.
D1 cha 142: Hmm... what kind of teachers... There are dozens of teachers, so each has their own character. If I had to pick one to talk about specially...
D2 cha 217: The head of our grade! He is a really funny PE teacher! His head is completely, shinily bald, and he is the kind of person who uses it as material to get the students laughing!
D3 cha 211: Last year's school festival was amazing! He and some student volunteers stuck suction cups on their foreheads and had a tug-of-war, pulling against each other.
D4 cha 227: Of course, the teacher won overwhelmingly. In an exhibition match, he took on the challenge of seeing how much weight he could pull with the suction cup.
D5 cha 198: In the end, he was pulling a cart with five female students on it. I was truly amazed that a suction cup on the forehead could do that.
D6 cha 232: For a while from the next day, the perfectly round red mark would not fade from his forehead. Even when he gave a speech at grade assemblies, the mood never got serious...
D7 cha 175: I am hoping he will do something at this year's school festival too.
E1 cha 166: The student council...? No, I think it is perfectly ordinary.
E2 cha 174: The student council president and officers are chosen by a school vote, and they decide things like school events and the club budgets.
E3 cha 191: It is by no means a powerful organization like in anime. Normally they are truly ordinary students.
E4 cha 278: Ahh, but... this might be a slightly odd tradition...
E5 cha 220: At the graduation ceremony, it has become customary for the student council to each take up an instrument and play a live band show. That too is something the student council started on its own.
E6 cha 175: So when first-years become council officers, they are often taken aback, not knowing about the custom. Being suddenly told to do band activities would be a problem, after all.
E7 cha 172: But when the graduation ceremony is over, the council members look really good. Like they have seen one big job through.
E8 cha 169: So I would think the student council's unity is stronger than at other schools. Is it not quite a unique student council?

キャプション1: Anything you want to ask me? 1
A1 cha 242: A question for /VAR/-sama, is it? If there is something I could ask now...
A2 cha 341: Which arc is your favorite?
キャプション2 cha 110: Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse] to Wabigoto Arc [Apology] (from the flayed-body case to the Megasawa City case)
キャプション3 cha 104: Shigatsu Arc [Death Month] to Saigo no Koe Arc [Last Voice] (the curse-killings in the Arata settlement)
キャプション4 cha 114: True Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse] to Eden no Sakura Arc [Eden's Cherry] (getting to the truth of Shigatsu Youka)
キャプション5: Eigo Kaiki Arc [Eternal Recurrence] (Haruka Niimura afterward)
B1 cha 226: Ho, so the early part is your number one favorite.
B2 cha 176: It is the opening section of this world, where every problem is raised. Perhaps /VAR/-sama likes stories where lots of unknown mysteries come up?
B3 cha 212: And yet even after that part ended, you kept watching this world for a long time, all the way to the final ending. I am deeply moved.
B4 cha 182: And that you still come to visit me like this even now is the greatest happiness there could be.
C1 cha 178: I see, the opening section involving the curse-killings.
C2 cha 204: Many very difficult stories, and yet you cannot easily reach the truth. To favor such arcs...
C3 cha 218: Could it be that /VAR/-sama enjoys being teased and kept waiting? Hee hee hee.
C4 cha 215: Still, it is the route that came about because the Megasawa City case was avoided. Compared with the early arcs, you can see the differences, which makes for quite an interesting way of viewing it.
C5 cha 180: And the colorful residents of the Arata settlement appear too. In that sense, could one call them gloomy yet lively arcs?
D1 cha 142: Ooh, so you like getting to the bottom of Shigatsu Youka. As every mystery gets solved, the fog lifts.
D2 cha 217: Also, just when the overall progress seemed to hit 100%, it turned out you were not even halfway. In that respect too, I think it was a shocking curtain-raiser.
D3 cha 211: Either way, in the end it is a route that solves the mysteries, stands up to the threat, and leads to a happy ending.
D4 cha 227: The smallest choice, and then a decision, lead to great courage to stand against tragedy. The power of the heart truly is a mysterious thing.
D5 cha 198: I am a different being from the Haruka Niimura of the route that defeated Shigatsu Youka, but I believe she and the others go on to live happy lives.
E2 cha 174: No, how shall I put it, it is a little embarrassing. After all, you saw me myself, plainly, and told me you liked it...
E3 cha 191: It is true that I killed Natsumi and fled into this world. I thought there was nothing more ahead for me.
E4 cha 278: But depending on how you think and what you choose, the future can be changed in any way. Even if you cannot choose, a road is always left. That is what I felt.
E5 cha 220: Whether that future turns out the worst, or turns out to be hope...
E6 cha 175: Hee hee, but it is embarrassing after all.

キャプション1: Anything you want to ask me? 2
A1 cha 242: A question for /VAR/-sama... Let me see...
A2 cha 341: Which system do you like best?
キャプション2 cha 110: Hidden Routes
B1 cha 226: Ooh, the hidden routes. That is rather hardcore.
B2 cha 176: I think you already know, but the hidden routes are scenarios added to this world later.
B3 cha 212: They take shape by switching a main-story scenario to another person's point of view, and I think they let you know the story more deeply.
B4 cha 182: /VAR/-sama too must have been surprised at times, thinking, "So this is what was going on behind this scenario."
B5 cha 171: Some hidden routes even get closer to the truth than the main-story scenarios. Hee hee hee.
C1 cha 178: Ho, the references. Then let me explain here why references were built into this world in the first place.
C2 cha 204: At first, the content of the references was going to be built into the main-story scenarios, but that produced a great many overly explanatory passages and scenes that tended to drag.
C3 cha 218: It began as separating those out, to keep down the impression of explaining and dragging.
C4 cha 215: Further, things hard to express in story form were classed as the object type. Rather than a story, they let you view what appeared just as it is, which made them easy to understand.
C5 cha 180: Also, the letter type and report type are formats added much later. Making them special types was so that /VAR/-sama would recognize them as special references.
C6 cha 237: Because of how this came about, you can glimpse the whole picture of this world to some degree without looking at the references at all. But you see that there is a difference in understanding between looking and not looking, do you not?
C7 cha 205: References were made in this way: important, but not getting in the way of the main-story scenarios.
D1 cha 142: The encyclopedia, is it? So that means /VAR/-sama has looked into quite fine details.
D2 cha 217: Then, it is a little meta, but let me tell you a secret hidden in this encyclopedia.
D3 cha 211: What is said to have been hardest in building the encyclopedia system is the New mark that tells 'seen' from 'not seen'.
D4 cha 227: Getting this New mark to display without bugs apparently took so much time it nearly brought tears.
D5 cha 198: And what is more, in writing that code, the symbol for joining strings, “++”, was used heavily.
D6 cha 232: So much so that when the author closed their eyes, the text “New++” was apparently burned into their vision.
D7 cha 175: New++... You have seen that somewhere, have you not?
D8 cha 201: Yes. That “New++”, stared at hundreds of times nearly in tears, became the circle's name just as it was.
D9 cha 153: And that was the rather disappointing origin of the circle name, which does not mean 'adding to something new'.
E1 cha 166: The chats! The chats! I am so happy! It means you are enjoying them right now.
E2 cha 174: This chat system was actually received far better than expected by a great many people, and I am surprised myself.
E3 cha 191: Some of them have nothing at all to do with this world, and a good many are shameless ones that could threaten my human rights...
E4 cha 278: In the sense that they let you refresh yourself, as a sort of palate cleanser, I think they have great reason to exist.
E5 cha 220: Incidentally, the reason the chat system was made was apparently "because even when the person inside is revealed, it is hard to feel much for her."
E6 cha 175: Well, if I only appeared in the gaps between scenarios, you would hardly take much interest in me...
E7 cha 172: To remedy that weakness, topics that tramp into my private life with their shoes on were apparently included on purpose...
E8 cha 169: Well, as things stand now, /VAR/-sama seems to have taken a great liking to them, so it all worked out in the end.

A1 cha 242: A question for /VAR/-sama... And then...
A2 cha 341: To be blunt, which did you think was bad about this work...?
キャプション2 cha 110: The scenarios are too long
キャプション5: I don't really get what the sect is

B2 cha 176: And on top of that, the unlock design means you cannot reach the ending of the Eigo Kaiki Arc [Eternal Recurrence] without properly viewing the references and chats.
B3 cha 212: I suspect that not even one in ten of all players has made it this far.
B4 cha 182: All the more reason I am grateful to /VAR/-sama for keeping me company this far.
B5 cha 171: Though I have said these thanks many times already. There is nothing more I can say.
C1 cha 178: Ngh... You have struck the sorest spot...
C2 cha 204: Yes, the creator is a beginner at drawing. The scenarios are text, and the sound uses free assets, so those parts can keep up a decent appearance, but...
C3 cha 218: The art is the one thing that cannot be faked. Character illustrations are not something you can use free assets for.
C4 cha 215: In fact, the characters being mainly silhouettes was apparently meant to reduce that weakness even a little.
C5 cha 180: This may sound high-handed, but this work is free, so if you could bear with it and turn a blind eye...
D1 cha 142: Indeed, the settings are rather complicated, in proportion to the volume.
D2 cha 217: /小/Honestly, it's because the creator never makes a plot outline...
D3 cha 211: /小/So the settings got patched on and on, and in the end even the creator couldn't make sense of them and had to go back over this whole long thing again and again...
D4 cha 227: /小/Fix a setting over there and one over here goes wrong, contradictions pile up...
D5 cha 198: /小/No wonder the settings ended up baffling the players...
D6 cha 232: Ah, no, I was just talking to myself.
D7 cha 175: There are many complicated settings, but the creator put heart and soul into making them, so I hope you will forgive them.
E1 cha 166: I see; it is only natural you would think so. It is a setting at the very foundation, and yet much about it is unclear.
E2 cha 174: But I am terribly sorry. For various reasons, the honest truth is that I cannot speak about it in detail.
E3 cha 191: So I would be glad if you could simply accept that such a sect existed.

キャプション1: Tell me just what you can about the Holy Cerejeira Church
A1 cha 242: Hmm, about this there really is little I can say for now.
A2 cha 341: If that is all right with you, I will tell you a little.
キャプション2 cha 110: Why is it connected to the state?
キャプション3 cha 104: Does it still exist as of 2020?
キャプション5: Could Droga be made in Megasawa City?
B1 cha 226: Akira Niimura once tried to present Droga to the shogun. A close aide of the shogun at that time had become a high official of the Meiji government.
B2 cha 176: He headed toward Iizawa Prefecture in search of Droga, which might help strengthen Japan's military.
B3 cha 212: But where he arrived was not the Arata settlement but Megasawa City. Megasawa City is the home base of the Holy Cerejeira Church.
B4 cha 182: The official came into contact with the Holy Cerejeira Church and was able to reach Droga. If one could get Droga, there was no need to go to the Arata settlement.
B5 cha 171: In this way the Holy Cerejeira Church gained a strong connection in a government official, and treated him generously as one of its leaders.
B6 cha 212: And with the official's efforts, by the time of the Showa era the Holy Cerejeira Church had built a system through which it could strongly influence the government.
B7 cha 169: However, the Holy Cerejeira Church's aim was only to worship Droga and keep its believers at peace, so it never tried to take power.
B8 cha 193: That is why it could even do something like lay a railway to the Arata settlement.
C1 cha 178: The Holy Cerejeira Church still exists in Megasawa City as of 2020.
C2 cha 204: However, it does not have the power it had when it was researching Droga. The believers number only a countable handful of households, I would think.
C3 cha 218: All the more so, the faith of today's believers seems very strong.
C4 cha 215: However, past research has already shown that Droga is dangerous. What on earth they take as their teaching is a mystery, but...
C5 cha 180: To give you just a little hint: it is what the Megasawa City case and Eiichiro Niimura's accidental death led to in the end.
D1 cha 142: This was depicted in the main story and references too, but around 1730, some residents of the Arata settlement opposed the ban on Droga.
D2 cha 217: Then they took the remaining Droga, left the settlement, and moved to Megasawa.
D3 cha 211: But Droga is extremely precious, and deciding who uses it and when becomes extremely important.
D4 cha 227: For that reason, the rules for using Droga were presumably very strict.
D5 cha 198: So they began to revere Droga as something precious. In other words, a religion with Droga as its sacred object came into being.
D6 cha 232: For believers of the Holy Cerejeira Church, being allowed to use Droga is a great honor, and the teaching came to be to build up virtue within the sect and earn the trust and respect of those around you so as to be chosen as a user.
D7 cha 175: But after the Edo period ended, wars began to break out frequently, and the idea spread that anyone should be able to use Droga in order to protect the believers.
D8 cha 201: So Droga came to be analyzed scientifically, and as a result it was found to be something that must not be used, and the Holy Cerejeira Church declined.
D9 cha 153: That is the founding and decline of the Holy Cerejeira Church.
E1 cha 166: They lived relying on Droga, so they must have sought places other than the Arata settlement where the cherries that become Droga, that is, Shigatsu Youka, grew wild.
E2 cha 174: In other words, Megasawa must have been a place where Shigatsu Youka grew wild. But nowhere in the main story is there any such description.
E3 cha 191: As a hint, you may figure it out if you consider what Shigatsu Youka was doing around 1730 for its true purpose.
E4 cha 278: As another hint, there is the geography of Megasawa. If you look carefully at the places in the encyclopedia, you may figure it out.
E5 cha 220: That said, I think guessing at this stage is difficult. Anything more is top secret.
